items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to registered pharmacy interns
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1043

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the education law, in relation to registered pharmacy
interns

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

Authorizes trained registered pharmacy interns to administer
immunization injections under the supervision of a licensed
pharmacist.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends subdivision 2 and subdivision 3 of section 6801 of
the education law to authorize a registered pharmacy intern to
administer immunization injections.

Section 2 adds a new subdivision 5 to section 6801 of the education
law to require that any licensed pharmacy intern administering an
injection only do so under the supervision of a licensed pharmacist.

Section 3 contains the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

New York is one of the few states which do not authorize registered
pharmacy interns to administer immunization injections. As of 2012, 35
states allowed such administration.

New York's pharmacy colleges are losing students to out of state
rotation programs due to the current state law. Normally, pharmacy
students participate in a rotation internship during the latter half
of their degree program. Without the ability to administer injections,
these students are denied the experience of administering an
injection. Instead, they must wait until they have already entered the
work force to learn how this essential skill in an applied setting.

This bill corrects this by authorizing registered pharmacies interns
to administer injections while under the direct supervisions of a
registered pharmacist. Students would have to attain a specific
certification or complete equivalent coursework before they were able
to administer such injections. This would provide a valuable learning
experience to pharmacy students while maintaining oversight.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S.7242/A.9312A of 2016; referred to Education.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that the
amendments made to section 6801 of the education law by section one of
this act shall not affect the expiration of such section and shall be
deemed expired therewith.
